The handler can return `Booking successfully cancelled` before those operations finish, and in a serverless/Next API route the runtime may freeze after the response, so the `cancelled: true` update at the core of this PR may never be persisted. The same fire-and-forget pattern appears in `handleNewBooking.ts:967`, `bookings.tsx:488`, and several `workflows.tsx` paths. If `client.request` throws, the catch logs the error and leaves the reminder with `cancelled` null and `scheduled` true. The cron retry logic only selects reminders where `cancelled: true`, so this reminder will never be cancelled and the scheduled email can still be delivered for a cancelled/rescheduled booking. This branch is used by reschedule and workflow/step deletion paths. On failure it should mark the reminder as canceled (or otherwise make it eligible for cron retry) instead of returning unchanged."

If a booking is cancelled close to the reminder's scheduled send time, the next cron run may happen after the send time, so the email will already have been delivered. This reintroduces the reported bug for a last-minute cancellation window. Reminders whose `scheduledDate` is within the next cron interval should be cancelled immediately, or the cron schedule/cutoff should guarantee cancellation before the send time."

Since these reminders are already within the next hour of their scheduled send, one transient error can cause multiple uncancelled emails to be delivered. Each reminder's cancel/delete should be handled independently so one failure does not prevent the rest from being cancelled."

findings.title: Reminder cancellation promises are not awaited
findings.body: `deleteScheduledEmailReminder` and `deleteScheduledSMSReminder` are async and perform database writes and external API calls, but they are fired inside nested `forEach` callbacks without collecting or awaiting the returned promises. The handler can return `Booking successfully cancelled` before those operations finish, and in a serverless/Next API route the runtime may freeze after the response, so the `cancelled: true` update at the core of this PR may never be persisted. The same fire-and-forget pattern appears in `handleNewBooking.ts:967`, `bookings.tsx:488`, and several `workflows.tsx` paths. Collect the promises and await them with `Promise.allSettled` before completing the handler.

findings.title: Immediate email cancellation has no retry/fallback on SendGrid failure
findings.body: In the `immediateDelete` branch, the function sends the SendGrid cancel request and then returns without deleting the `WorkflowReminder` row or setting `cancelled: true`. If `client.request` throws, the catch logs the error and leaves the reminder with `cancelled` null and `scheduled` true. The cron retry logic only selects reminders where `cancelled: true`, so this reminder will never be cancelled and the scheduled email can still be delivered for a cancelled/rescheduled booking. This branch is used by reschedule and workflow/step deletion paths. On failure it should mark the reminder as canceled (or otherwise make it eligible for cron retry) instead of returning unchanged.

findings.title: Non-immediate cancellation can be too late for near-term scheduled sends
findings.body: For the non-immediate path, the function only sets `cancelled: true`; the actual SendGrid cancel happens later in the 15-minute cron when the scheduled date is within the next hour. If a booking is cancelled close to the reminder's scheduled send time, the next cron run may happen after the send time, so the email will already have been delivered. This reintroduces the reported bug for a last-minute cancellation window. Reminders whose `scheduledDate` is within the next cron interval should be cancelled immediately, or the cron schedule/cutoff should guarantee cancellation before the send time.

findings.title: One SendGrid cancellation error blocks all other cancellations in the batch
findings.body: The whole `for` loop over `remindersToCancel` is wrapped in a single `try/catch`. If any single `client.request` fails, control jumps to the catch, logs, and skips all remaining selected reminders until the next cron run. Since these reminders are already within the next hour of their scheduled send, one transient error can cause multiple uncancelled emails to be delivered. Each reminder's cancel/delete should be handled independently so one failure does not prevent the rest from being cancelled.

findings.title: No tests were added for the new cancellation behavior
findings.body: The PR changes the cancellation model for workflow email reminders, including the new `cancelled` field, deferred SendGrid cancellation in the cron, immediate-delete call paths, and SMS deletion. No tests cover these paths. A regression here would silently send workflow emails for cancelled or rescheduled bookings, which is the exact user-facing bug being fixed. Add unit/integration tests for marking reminders cancelled, cron retrieval within the one-hour window, SendGrid cancel failures, and SMS cancellation.
